concerns.text: FR-006 adds a multiple‑comparison correction (Benjamini‑Hochberg) which was not part of the original idea. The idea only asks for measuring fidelity; correction for multiple tests is not explicitly required and constitutes an over‑reach beyond the stated scope.

FR-007 introduces a sensitivity‑analysis sweeping significance thresholds and reporting classification stability. The original research question does not call for threshold‑sweeping or binary ‘faithful/unfaithful’ classification, so this expands the scope.

FR-014 requires generation of KDE PDFs, side‑by‑side histograms, QQ‑plots, and heatmaps as visual artifacts. The idea only demands quantitative comparison of statistical properties; visualisation requirements are not requested and add unnecessary work.

FR-018 mandates paired significance testing (t‑test or Wilcoxon) to claim overall superiority of a method. The idea does not seek a ranking or superiority claim, only a measurement of fidelity, so this is an over‑reach.

FR-019 defines a random‑noise baseline dataset for SC‑003 comparisons. The original idea never mentions a baseline; this adds a new experimental condition not required for answering the research question.

FR-020 introduces a binary ‘faithful’ vs ‘unfaithful’ column classification based on p‑value and effect‑size thresholds. The idea does not ask for binary labeling; it only asks for measuring how well distributions are reproduced.

FR-021 specifies a control‑perturbation dataset (column‑wise permutation) as a ground‑truth reference for false‑positive/false‑negative rates. This construct was not present in the idea and changes the evaluation methodology.
FR-022 requires reporting false‑positive and false‑negative rates using the control‑perturbation dataset. Since FR‑021 is itself out of scope, this downstream requirement also over‑reaches.

The spec implicitly redefines the research question from “to what extent do summary statistics, correlation structures, and distributional shapes … faithfully reproduce” to a binary classification problem with threshold‑sweeping and error‑rate reporting. This drift changes the nature of the inquiry and is not justified by the original idea.
